propositions: A pure evidence-prepacked single-pass verifier produces false-positive rejections when the prepack is imperfect; a filter-only stage (PASS or ABSTAIN, never FAIL) combined with narrowed agentic fallback eliminates false-positive rejection by construction.

Filter+fallback on six corpus tickets (3 real, 3 adversarial with planted-unmet ACs) achieves -26% total input tokens and -46% on real tickets versus pure-agentic control, with zero false PASSes on adversarial ACs.

Filter coverage is bimodal by AC style: ACs naming greppable artifacts (symbols, files, tests) PASS ~90%; ACs asserting runtime outcomes or store-side artifacts ABSTAIN, reducing filter usefulness to ~39% real-ticket ACs but preserving correctness.

The agentic verifier itself exhibits low-rate false-FAIL variance (2 genuinely-met ACs failed in one run), which the narrowing design does not eliminate but the filter+fallback combination makes tolerable via the cost savings.

Prepacking must deterministically assemble evidence (grep-at-ref, file_impact slices, referencing commits, test function listings) with cap-on-missing and never-synthesize discipline; filter contract enforced as PASS-with-citations or ABSTAIN, forbidding FAIL.

Productization requires: AC-block rewrite seam for criteria reduction, filter-PASS citations recorded in verdict, coverage telemetry per AC style to skip the filter call on runtime-outcome-heavy tickets, and re-validation of the 8000-char description admission cap after reduction.
